name: cold_roofing_v1
hypothesis: Domestic roofers reply to the old-quotes offer at least as well as window installers, and the free-first-50 offer beats pay-per-booked-survey for them too. Same two offers as cold_offer_v1 so the trades can be compared like for like.
variable: offer paragraph and ask in the first email (subject, opener and follow-ups identical); trade compared against cold_offer_v1
decision_rule: After min_sent_per_arm first emails per arm: compare the trade's overall positive-reply rate with windows (cold_offer_v1). If roofing is not clearly worse, keep sending roofers and keep the better arm (>= 90% probability); if neither arm reaches 90%, keep the one with more booked calls.

arms.subject: last year's roof quotes
arms.body:
Hi,

Ever had a homeowner ring back months after a roof quote, usually after the next leak?

The ones who never ring back are still sitting in {company}'s inbox. You've already paid for them: the lead, the trip out, the pricing.

I chase them in your name and put anyone still keen in your diary. You only pay for surveys that get booked.

Worth a look?

follow_ups.2:
Hi,

The usual worry is annoying old customers, so here's exactly what they'd get, from your name:

"Hi, it's {company}. We quoted you for your roof a while back. Did you ever get it sorted?"

That's it. Anyone who says not yet gets offered a survey. Anyone who says no is left alone.

Roughly how many old quotes have you got: tens, hundreds?
